chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Iyyad ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a slave who had children from a free woman, and he freed him. He said: 'The manumission bond (walā') of his children belongs to the one who freed him.'

key_terms.أَوْلاَدٌ: Children; specifically referring to offspring from a mixed-status union.
key_terms.اِمْرَأَةٍ حُرَّةٍ: A free woman; indicating the mother was not a slave, making the child free but with specific inheritance/patronage rules.
key_terms.فَأَعْتَقَهُ: And he freed him; referring to the act of manumitting the slave father.
key_terms.وَلَاءُ: Manumission bond; the right of patronage and inheritance between a freed person and their former master.

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the manumission bond (walā') of children born to a slave from a free mother when the father is freed?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the specific application of the emancipation bond (walā') for children of mixed status (umm walad) when their father is manumitted, ruling that the patronage rights transfer to the father's master rather than the mother's. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the father's lineage and manumission status in determining inheritance of walā', distinguishing it from cases where the mother alone is freed. It underscores the legal principle that the bond follows the primary act of manumission, ensuring clarity in property and inheritance distribution within the family structure.
